defs: v	Misspelling of receive. [(transitive) To be given, sent, or paid something.]
v	(transitive) To ease (a person, person's thoughts etc.) from mental distress; to stop (someone) feeling anxious or worried, to alleviate the distress of.
v	(transitive) To ease (someone, a part of the body etc.) or give relief from physical pain or discomfort.
v	(transitive) To alleviate (pain, distress, mental discomfort etc.).
v	(transitive) To provide comfort or assistance to (someone in need, especially in poverty).
v	(transitive) To bring military help to (a besieged town); to lift the siege on.
v	(law) To free (someone) from debt or legal obligations; to give legal relief to.
v	To release (someone) from or of a difficulty, unwanted task, responsibility etc.
v	(originally military) To free (someone) from their post, task etc. by taking their place.
v	(reflexive, euphemistic) To urinate or defecate.
v	(reflexive, euphemistic) To ease one's own desire to orgasm, often through masturbation to orgasm.
v	(now rare) To raise (someone) out of danger or from (a specified difficulty etc.).
v	(now rare) To make (something) stand out; to make prominent, bring into relief.
v	(obsolete) To lift up; to raise again.
v	Misspelling of deceive. [(transitive) To trick or mislead.]
